title: Product framing: Station Air Risk with two modes
context: The course needs a Spark ML chain. We want a product that serves real users.
decision: Build one pipeline that gives a risk class per station and hour, in a short-term mode and an outlook mode, plus a data-trust flag.
rivals: R1: regression of the PM10 level. R2: data-quality and anomaly detection product. R3: station comparison and benchmark product.
evidence: H-01 and H-02 are not tested yet. H-06 is not tested yet.
refutation: H-01 refuted: drop the outlook mode. H-02 refuted: drop the short-term mode. H-06 refuted: evaluate R2 and R3.
consequences: Two feature sets and two model comparisons are needed. The talk must show which modes are not refuted.

title: ML family: classification
context: Users take act or do-not-act decisions (assumed, G-15).
decision: Predict a risk class (high or not high).
rivals: R1: regression of PM10, then a threshold. R2: more than two classes.
refutation: A source or user shows that users need a level and not a class. Then evaluate R1.
consequences: Metrics are classification metrics. A threshold is needed (D-003).

title: Target threshold method
context: No legal limit exists for underground rail spaces. The class needs a threshold.
decision: High means PM10 above the 75th percentile of PM10 on the training period only.
rivals: R1: a health reference value (ANSES, G-14). R2: a percentile per station.
evidence: No evidence yet. The percentile is a relative rule. It does not mean a health risk.
refutation: G-14 closes with a reference that users apply. Then evaluate R1. Results for R1 are also reported as a sensitivity check.
consequences: The label is computed after the split, on training data only, to avoid leakage.

title: Prediction horizons
decision: Short-term mode: horizons 1 hour and 24 hours. Outlook mode: any future hour, calendar features only.
rivals: R1: one horizon only (1 hour). R2: daily class instead of hourly.
evidence: H-01 and H-02 are not tested yet.
refutation: See D-001. If skill at 24 hours is not better than the outlook mode, keep 1 hour only.
consequences: Features must use only data available at prediction time for each horizon.

title: Chronological split
context: Time series. Random splits leak future information.
decision: Train up to 2024-12-31. Validation 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30. Test 2025-07-01 to the last date. Test used once.
rivals: R1: rolling-origin validation with several folds. R2: split dates per station.
evidence: G-18 is open: stations NPT and DGA have short histories.
refutation: G-18 shows that a station has too few training hours. Then evaluate R2 or exclude the station from that mode and say so.
consequences: Dates are recorded in the pre-registration sheet before modelling.

title: Metrics, baselines and failure line
context: Metrics chosen after results cause bias.
decision: Primary: F1 of class high. Guardrails: recall and precision of class high, area under PR curve, results per station. Baselines: persistence (short-term), same hour-of-week class on training data (outlook), station base rate (both).
rivals: R1: F2 score (recall weighted) if G-15 shows that missed highs cost more. R2: area under PR curve as primary.
refutation: G-15 closes with a cost ratio that is not near 1. Then evaluate R1. The switch is logged before the test period is used.
consequences: All values are fixed and dated in the pre-registration sheet.

title: Algorithms
context: The brief asks for at least two ML algorithms.
decision: LogisticRegression (simple, readable coefficients) and RandomForestClassifier (non-linear). GBTClassifier only if time is left.
rivals: R1: GBTClassifier instead of RandomForestClassifier. R2: one model per station.
evidence: Brief requirement. No performance evidence yet.
refutation: If both models do not do better than the baselines, we report this result and do not add models to find a better number.
consequences: Hyperparameter search space is fixed in the pre-registration sheet.

title: Spark ML for the whole chain
context: The brief asks for Transformers, Estimators, a Pipeline and an evaluation in Spark.
decision: All processing and modelling use Spark. pandas is used only to draw plots from small aggregated results.
rivals: R1: pandas or scikit-learn for parts of the chain.
refutation: Not applicable. This is a course constraint.
consequences: The notebook must run on the Docker Spark cluster.

title: Flag, do not delete
context: Data quality rules are not validated (G-07 to G-11).
decision: Quality rules add flag columns in Silver. They do not delete or change values. Each model run states which flags it excludes.
rivals: R1: delete invalid rows. R2: replace invalid values with estimates.
evidence: Notebook section 4 lists candidate rules. Causes are not known.
refutation: Not applicable. This keeps all options open. Each rule can change when a gap closes.
consequences: Each exclusion is a parameter of the run and is reported.

title: Dataset choice
context: The brief asks for a CSV dataset that we describe.
decision: Use the SNCF air-quality dataset. It is real, open, time-based, messy and multi-station.
rivals: R1: RATP per-station air data (S-08). R2: a clean tabular dataset from a teaching repository.
evidence: The data loads and has more than 200000 rows (notebook section 1).
refutation: G-13 shows that the licence does not allow reuse. Then evaluate R1.
consequences: Data cleaning and source search are part of the work, not a delay.

title: Document format
context: Documents must be readable without tools and easy to update.
decision: LaTeX sources, built with latexmk through a Makefile. Built PDFs are committed. Registers are CSV files.
consequences: Run make in docs after each change. Registers are edited as CSV.

title: Writing standard
context: Readers can have different English levels.
decision: Write about 80 percent of the text in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
consequences: See the writing rules (Product Charter, Appendix A).

title: Course brief location
context: The brief was in the docs root.
rivals: R1: keep it in the docs root.
consequences: Links to the brief use docs/reference/DaSci_BDA_Projet.pdf.

title: Raw data is never changed
context: Changing source files makes errors impossible to trace.
decision: spark/data/ is a raw zone. No job writes there. Processing writes to a separate store (spark/lake/bronze, silver, gold). Each raw file has a manifest entry.
refutation: Not applicable. Enforcement with a read-only mount is PROPOSED and needs approval.
consequences: The notebook must read from spark/data/ and write only to spark/lake/.

title: Source discovery before modelling
context: The SNCF file is one output of a larger measurement system. Other sources can close gaps or contradict our framing.
decision: Search and record sources before feature work. Add a source only if it serves a gap or hypothesis and fits the one-week scope.
rivals: R1: use only the current file.
evidence: Search results on 2026-11-27 show partners and related data (see source register).
consequences: The source register keeps rejected sources and the reason.
